CODELEARN · F7 — CHAPTER QUIZ

FER202 final assignment (mini LMS) · Function 7 of 11 · Starter = reference of F6 · Suggested time: 120 minutes · Total: 10 marks

1. Overview

Every chapter ends with a quiz made of all questions whose chapterId is that chapter. The student picks one option per question (radio buttons), submits, and sees the score; 70% or more passes. After submitting, every question shows whether it was right, highlights the correct option, crosses out a wrong choice and shows the explanation. Each attempt is stored in results so F8 can show the history. "Retake quiz" clears the answers.

API calls

WhenRequest
open /quiz/:chapterIdGET /chapters/:id (title + courseId) and GET /questions?chapterId=:id; enrolments of the student (F5)
submitPOST /results { userId, courseId, chapterId, score, total, percent, passed, answers: [optionIndex…], submittedAt }

Scoring: score = number of questions where the chosen index === answerIndex; percent = Math.round(score / total × 100); passed = percent ≥ 70. (json-server sends answerIndex to the browser — a real back end would grade on the server; expect that question in the defence.)

Edge cases

  • Submit with unanswered questions ⇒ #quiz-error "Please answer all questions (N unanswered)." and no request.
  • Not enrolled in the chapter's course ⇒ #not-enrolled; chapter without questions ⇒ #no-questions; unknown chapter ⇒ #quiz-not-found.
  • After submitting, options are locked until "Retake quiz". Opening another chapter starts clean.

Main features

  • Load & guard · Answering & validation · Score & save · Review & retake · Links & slice

General requirements

  • Continue from your own F6 code (or the starter, which is the F6 reference). Files marked NEW/EDIT in the tree are the ones this step touches.
  • Create React App (React 18), React Router v6, Redux Toolkit, Axios, React-Bootstrap; json-server 0.17.4 on port 9999 (1.x dropped _expand/_embed).
  • Every HTTP call goes through src/api/*.js (one axiosClient with baseURL: process.env.REACT_APP_API_URL); each API function returns response.data itself — do not rely on interceptors (the auto-grader’s axios does not run them).
  • Keep the ids/classes printed in the brief — the auto-grader uses them. Components never call axios directly.

4. Data model

db.json — 8 collections (json-server 0.17.4, port 9999)

FieldTypeNotes

5. Functional requirements

1. Load & guard 2 marks

Requirements:

  • Protected route /quiz/:chapterId: #quiz-title "Quiz: <chapter title>", one .question#q-<id> per question with .question-text "N. content". Guards: #not-enrolled, #no-questions, #quiz-not-found.

Must use: useParams Promise.all

2. Answering & validation 2 marks

Requirements:

  • Radio inputs #q<questionId>-o<optionIndex> (e.g. #q1-o1), one group per question (name); answers kept in the store as { [questionId]: optionIndex }. Submitting #quiz-form with gaps ⇒ #quiz-error, no POST.

Must use: Form.Check type="radio"

3. Score & save 3 marks

Requirements:

  • #quiz-result "You scored S/T (P%) — Passed 🎉" or "— Not passed"; the attempt is POSTed to results with numbers and booleans (not strings).

Must use: createAsyncThunk getState

Example:

q1 ✓, q2 ✗, q3 ✓ ⇒ "You scored 2/3 (67%) — Not passed" · POST /results { score: 2, total: 3, percent: 67, passed: false, answers: [1, 0, 0] }

4. Review & retake 2 marks

Requirements:

  • After submitting: each .question gets correct or incorrect; the right option has option-correct, a wrong pick option-wrong; .explanation appears; inputs are disabled. #retake-quiz clears answers and result.

5. Links & slice 1 mark

Requirements:

  • Learn page sidebar: .chapter-quiz#quiz-link-<chapterId> under every chapter. features/quiz/quizSlice.js: fetchQuiz, submitQuiz, reducers answerSelected, retakeQuiz; pure scoreQuiz() in utils/learning.js.

6. Element ids / classes used by the auto-grader

SelectorPurpose
#quiz-title #quiz-form .question#q-ID .question-text #qQID-oNquiz form
#submit-quiz #quiz-error #quiz-result #retake-quiz #quiz-save-error #back-to-learnactions + messages
.correct .incorrect .option-correct .option-wrong .explanationreview classes
#not-enrolled #no-questions #quiz-not-found · .chapter-quiz#quiz-link-IDguards + links

7. Grading rubric

#FeatureMarks
1Load & guard2
2Answering & validation2
3Score & save3
4Review & retake2
5Links & slice1
Total10

Common deductions

  • Comparing the chosen option as a string ("1") with answerIndex (number) ⇒ every answer counted wrong.
  • Score shown but never saved (F8 has nothing to show).
  • Hard-coded http://localhost:9999 in components instead of the .env variable.
  • Mutating Redux/React state, or writing localStorage inside a reducer.
  • App crashes (white screen) on an empty list, an unknown id or a server error.

8. Submission

Work in the editor (files on the right) or download the starter, then npm install and npm run dev (json-server :9999 + React :3000) and paste your files back. Press Run for the sample checks and Submit for full grading (hidden checks included). The reference solution of this step unlocks after an Accepted submission.

Assignment cuối kỳ FER202 (mini LMS) · Chức năng 7/11 · Starter = lời giải F6 · Thời gian gợi ý: 120 phút · Tổng: 10 điểm

1. Tổng quan

Mỗi chương kết thúc bằng một quiz gồm mọi câu hỏi có chapterId là chương đó. Học viên chọn một phương án mỗi câu (radio), nộp, và xem điểm; từ 70% là đạt. Sau khi nộp, từng câu cho biết đúng hay sai, tô đáp án đúng, gạch lựa chọn sai và hiện giải thích. Mỗi lượt làm lưu vào results để F8 hiện lịch sử. "Retake quiz" xoá câu trả lời.

Lời gọi API

Khi nàoRequest
mở /quiz/:chapterIdGET /chapters/:id (tên + courseId) và GET /questions?chapterId=:id; lượt ghi danh của học viên (F5)
nộpPOST /results { userId, courseId, chapterId, score, total, percent, passed, answers: [chỉ số phương án…], submittedAt }

Chấm: score = số câu có chỉ số đã chọn === answerIndex; percent = Math.round(score / total × 100); passed = percent ≥ 70. (json-server gửi cả answerIndex về trình duyệt — back end thật phải chấm ở máy chủ; GV hay hỏi câu này khi bảo vệ.)

Trường hợp biên

  • Nộp khi còn câu chưa trả lời ⇒ #quiz-error "Please answer all questions (N unanswered)." và không gửi request.
  • Chưa ghi danh khoá của chương ⇒ #not-enrolled; chương chưa có câu hỏi ⇒ #no-questions; chương lạ ⇒ #quiz-not-found.
  • Đã nộp thì khoá lựa chọn cho tới khi "Retake quiz". Mở chương khác thì bắt đầu sạch.

Chức năng chính

  • Tải & chặn · Trả lời & kiểm · Chấm & lưu · Xem lại & làm lại · Link & slice

Yêu cầu chung

  • Create React App (React 18), React Router v6, Redux Toolkit, Axios, React-Bootstrap; json-server 0.17.4 cổng 9999 (bản 1.x bỏ _expand/_embed).
  • Mọi lời gọi HTTP đi qua src/api/*.js (một axiosClient với baseURL: process.env.REACT_APP_API_URL); mỗi hàm API tự trả response.data — đừng dựa vào interceptor (axios của máy chấm không chạy interceptor).
  • Giữ đúng id/class in trong đề — máy chấm dùng chúng. Component không gọi axios trực tiếp.

```bash
npm install              # React 18 is pinned: CRA now installs React 19 by default (peer conflicts)
```

exercises.solutionExplanationHtml: Walkthrough. fetchQuiz loads the chapter and its questions together; its pending case wipes the previous attempt. Answers live in the store as a map keyed by question id, written by a plain reducer, so the radios are fully controlled and "Retake" is just a reset. Submitting first counts unanswered questions locally (no request), then submitQuiz reads the questions and answers with getState(), scores them with the pure scoreQuiz, and saves the attempt; the saved row becomes result, which drives the result alert, the correct/incorrect classes, the highlighted options and the explanations. The page also checks the enrolment of the chapter's course, so typing the URL does not bypass enrolment.

Câu trả lời nằm trong store dạng map theo id câu hỏi, ghi bằng reducer thường ⇒ radio hoàn toàn controlled và "Retake" chỉ là đặt lại. Khi nộp, trước tiên đếm câu chưa trả lời ngay ở client (không gửi request), rồi submitQuiz đọc câu hỏi + câu trả lời bằng getState(), chấm bằng hàm thuần scoreQuiz và lưu lượt làm; bản ghi đã lưu thành result, từ đó suy ra thông báo điểm, class correct/incorrect, phương án được tô và giải thích. Trang còn kiểm ghi danh khoá của chương nên gõ URL cũng không vượt được.

lessons.title: What is React?
lessons.content:
React is a JavaScript library for building user interfaces from small, reusable components.
In this lesson you see how a React app is just a tree of components that turn data into UI.

lessons.title: Create React App & project structure
lessons.content:
Create the project with npx create-react-app, then walk through public/index.html, src/index.js and src/App.js.
Run it with npm start on http://localhost:3000.

lessons.title: JSX and components
lessons.content:
JSX looks like HTML but compiles to React.createElement calls.
A component is a function that returns JSX; its name must start with a capital letter.

lessons.title: Props vs State
lessons.content:
Props are read-only data passed from a parent; state is data a component owns and changes with its setter.
Changing state re-renders the component.

lessons.title: useState and useEffect
lessons.content:
useState stores a value between renders; useEffect runs side effects such as fetching data after the component renders.
Always list the values the effect uses in its dependency array.

lessons.title: let, const and var
lessons.content: Prefer const, use let when a variable must be reassigned, and avoid var (function scope, hoisting surprises).

lessons.title: Primitive types
lessons.content: string, number, boolean, null, undefined, bigint and symbol — and why typeof null is "object".

lessons.title: Arrow functions and array methods
lessons.content: Write short callbacks with arrow functions and transform data with map, filter and reduce without mutating the original array.

lessons.title: Your first Express server
lessons.content: Install express, create an app and call app.listen(3000). Add a GET route that returns JSON.

lessons.title: Routing & middleware
lessons.content: Split routes with express.Router and write middleware with (req, res, next) for logging and validation.

lessons.title: Building a REST API
lessons.content: Map CRUD to HTTP: GET /items, POST /items, PUT /items/:id, DELETE /items/:id — with the right status codes.

lessons.title: SELECT, WHERE, ORDER BY
lessons.content: Choose columns with SELECT, filter rows with WHERE and sort the result with ORDER BY.

lessons.title: JOIN in practice
lessons.content: Combine rows of related tables with INNER JOIN and LEFT JOIN on their keys.

options: React compares references, so the same array means no re-render
questions.explanation: Create a new array/object (spread, map, filter) so React sees a new reference and re-renders.

options: In their closest common parent (lift state up)

questions.content: What is wrong with calling a hook inside an if statement?
options: Hooks must be called in the same order on every render
Hooks only work in class components
questions.explanation: React matches hook state by call order, so hooks must sit at the top level of the component.

questions.content: Which keyword declares a variable that cannot be reassigned?
questions.explanation: const prevents reassignment (the object it points to can still change).

questions.content: What is typeof null in JavaScript?
questions.explanation: A historic bug kept for compatibility: typeof null === "object".
Any non-empty string, including "0", is truthy.

questions.explanation: app.listen(port, callback) opens the HTTP server.

questions.content: What does an Express middleware function receive?
